_comment: WHAT THE OWNER CHOSE. What each source's own published TERMS require is
not here: it is in packages/sources/src/terms.ts, quoted from the vendor's
documents. Keeping the two apart is what lets this system detect a source
configured WITHOUT a ceiling its terms declare - if both facts lived in
this file, an absent ceiling and a source with no ceiling would be the
same document.
Nothing here has a built-in default. A source missing a required setting
does not run, and the refusal names the source and the setting.
Keys beginning with an underscore are comments and are ignored.
One entry per source this system may read. Every source named here must
also carry a host ceiling and, where its vendor publishes a limit, a
metered allowance in config/governor.json - the governor's first two
gates refuse an unconfigured host and an unknown source.
The one retailer that publishes an official API.
baseUrl is the documented API root; a single-product call is built
under it as /products/<sku>.json.
currency and timeZone are DECLARATIONS and not readings: the vendor's
documentation publishes neither anywhere. The currency decides the
ISO 4217 minor-unit exponent, so getting it wrong is a wrong NUMBER
and not a wrong label; the time zone is stored beside every instant
because a 90-day low is anchored to the retailer's local day, and it
is also how a zone-less priceUpdateDate becomes an instant at all.
rawContextRetentionHours is 24, well inside the 72 hours the terms
permit cached Content to be held: this system needs the raw payload
only long enough to debug a mapping break, and holding less than a
third party permits is always allowed while holding more never is.
credentialVariable names the environment variable the API key is read
from. The key itself is never in this file, never in a stored row,
never in a notification body and never in a log line.
